data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject only when the test's failure path is itself subject to mutation testing; otherwise the test can be a description wearing a guard's uniform, and the asymmetry (1/9 vs 4/4 to 6/7) arises because the failing-mutation ritual for compile.py was applied to the compiler's own guard logic while the other modules' guards were never shown a fail-first installation.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the mutation testing framework excludes the test's own guard logic from mutation, this asymmetry disappears.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If compile.py's lost mutation was in a different file from the other 9, the result is confounded.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 4/4 to 6/7 modules had fewer mutation opportunities per guard, the ratio is an artifact of registry size.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the author ran the mutation suite in a different order for different modules, installation-first ordering is not the cause.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Shown-to-fail-first installation forces the test's own failure path to be exercised. In compile.py, the one mutation that was lost was lost because the guard that should have caught it was itself the mutated subject. In the other modules, 4/4 to 6/7 guards fired because they were installed after the code they guarded, so the mutations were caught by guards that had never been shown to fail. The 3-of-26 distribution is a property of which guard was installed first, not of which code was mutated.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
